item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit. 99dd5b5e changes exactly the two docstrings in reckon/crew/dispatch.py (both hunks fall inside docstring text at :5626 and :5663; no statement of the function is touched) and adds one test plus its mutation hook. bde4b2f0 adds only the landing fragment and its figure, both new files. The base-to-head diff of dispatch.py is therefore a textual claim change and nothing else, which the reviewer's own probe at both revisions confirms behaviourally.
item_verdicts.done_when: Section 6's measure is asserted by tests/test_worker_scratch_lives_with_its_run.py, whose module docstring now lists the moved-root property among the properties it covers. My independent runs at bde4b2f0 in a scratch tree (logs/after-independent.log, module.__file__ and cwd on the header lines) are 14 passed in 11.91s, matching the reviewed run's gates/after.log 14 passed; my independent base arm at 13f950ff (logs/base-independent.log, RECKON_RUN_ID unset) is 13 passed, matching gates/base.log. Under the declared mutation RECKON_WORKER_SCRATCH_MOVED_NEGATIVE=1 my own run reproduces exactly the promised red set: 2 failed, 12 passed, with test_a_recorded_path_outside_the_root_is_withheld and test_a_record_under_a_moved_root_is_withheld red (logs/negative-control-independent.log).
item_verdicts.goal: The goal — a scratch-removal docstring that states the moved-root refusal the code actually makes — holds at bde4b2f0. My probe (logs/probe.log, run against the scratch tree at bde4b2f0 with the module path printed) created a run's scratch under root A, redirected RECKON_WORKER_SCRATCH_ROOT to root B, and called remove_worker_scratch with the recorded path: removed False, withheld 'scratch path is not the directory this run owns', the directory still present, its payload intact. The positive control in the same probe (same call without the move) removed the directory and printed it, so the withholds are refusals rather than a broken call site. The same probe against 13f950ff (logs/probe-base.log) returns the identical result, so the behaviour was already correct and the wrong claim was the docstring's, exactly as the manifest states.

The commands' summaries are 13 passed and 14 passed with EXIT=0, matching the manifest's claims, and my own independent arms reproduce both counts. commits names 99dd5b5e and bde4b2f0, both reachable with bde4b2f0 the worktree head; changed_paths lists the 4 paths the base-to-head diffstat lists, and the worktree is clean at the head. The declared mutation string appears verbatim as the first line of gates/negative_control.log.
item_verdicts.write_paths: git diff --stat 13f950ff bde4b2f0 lists exactly reckon/crew/dispatch.py, tests/test_worker_scratch_lives_with_its_run.py, docs/evidence/fragments/a-worker-knows-it-is-on-compute/scratch-docstring-states-the-refusal.html and docs/figures/a-worker-knows-it-is-on-compute/scratch-docstring-states-the-refusal/scratch-moved-root-withheld.svg — the four paths the manifest declares, with no path touched outside the declared scope. The worktree is clean at bde4b2f0. The fragment is a legitimate landing anchor at this head: reckon/resources.py:222 _is_evidence_fragment walks past the evidence/fragments subtree at :232, before the typed-root refusal at :238, so the file it adds does not re-open the failure commit ae10dc0b withdrew a fragment for; my call of _path_context on the fragment's relative path returns (None, False, False) while the control path plans/a-worker-knows-it-is-on-compute/extra.html still raises ResourceCollision, so the acceptance is specific rather than a blanket pass.

justifications.durability: The property the docstring now states is guarded rather than merely asserted: under the declared mutation the new case reddens together with the outside-the-root case, and my own run of that mutation reproduces the exact red set, so the sentence names a refusal a test defends. One deduction: the test locks the behaviour, not the wording — the old claim could be restored to the docstring with nothing failing, so the wording itself remains review-guarded only.
justifications.evidence: Every claim in the manifest was independently reproduced from the reviewed head: the after arm 14 passed and the base arm 13 passed in my own scratch trees at bde4b2f0 and 13f950ff with module.__file__ and cwd on the log headers, the declared negative control reddening exactly the two named cases, the derivation of 0 added failures over the reviewed run's own gate logs with controls that see an injected id, ignore a shared one and read an absent head log as unmeasured, and the moved-root refusal itself reproduced by a probe that also carries its positive control. base_test_worker_scratch_lives_with_its_run.py in the gates directory is byte-identical to the base revision's test file (sha256 5e59315b), so the base arm is the base. One deduction: after_copy.py in the same directory is a pre-format copy rather than the head artifact (finding above).
justifications.fit: The rewritten text states the mechanism rather than the history: the guard's docstring names the parent-of-the-current-root requirement and the withhold, and remove_worker_scratch's names the same consequence for a moved root, with no plan, ticket or stage identifier and no attribution. The new identifiers (_accept_moved_root, _observed_moved_root, MOVED_ROOT_CONTROL_MUTATION, test_a_record_under_a_moved_root_is_withheld) are named for what they do and match the file's existing convention. The change adds no ruff finding to either staged path (dispatch.py 7 findings at base and 7 at head, all at lines 1-5014, none inside the edited docstrings at :5626-:5675) and the new test file is at 0 findings and formatted.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The one claim the node set out to repair was reproduced in both directions: the docstring's old sentence ('its value is resilience to a root that moved') is falsified by the probe at both revisions — the guard withholds rather than uses the record — and the new sentence's claim (withheld and left in place, never removed) is confirmed by the same probe with a positive control showing the instrument still removes a directory it owns. The base-to-head diff of the module is docstring text only, so nothing else about the removal moved while the wording changed.
justifications.scope_discipline: The endpoint diff lists exactly the four declared paths, the worktree is clean at the reviewed head, and both commits are conventional with bodies, free of AI attribution and of plan, sprint or ticket identifiers. No file outside the declared scope was written, and the fragment the node added is supported by the reader at this head (verified with a control that still refuses a genuinely reserved path shape).
